Selected path: first-time applicants studying the standard Class C license material; commercial endorsements are excluded. [A08]
Official question count remains unknown (verify ME-SEC07-COUNT); official passing standard remains unknown (verify ME-SEC07-PASS); official time limit remains unknown (verify ME-SEC07-TIME).
This dossier’s subject is General Driving; the source map controls coverage rather than an invented official exam weight.

sections.heading: B — General Driving
sections.markdown:
## B — General Driving
Audience: English-language first-time standard-license applicants using the General Driving section.
Level: beginner study of the selected handbook material, followed by recall and application practice.
Prerequisite policy: understand the cited terminology before comparing exceptions; this is a teaching order, not an extra licensing eligibility requirement.
Coverage basis: the physical source range and the fact roster define this topic; no official topic percentage was supplied.

## C — General Driving

FACT_ID: sec07-F01 | anchor: A61
Before a turn, check controls, pedestrians and vehicles, signal, and enter the nearest lane in the intended direction. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec07-F02 | anchor: A61
Look through the turn as far as possible, accelerate smoothly and ensure the signal cancels afterward. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec07-F03 | anchor: A61
Start a right turn from the rightmost part of your lane without swinging left first. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec07-F04 | anchor: A61
Start a left turn from the leftmost part of your lane and yield to oncoming traffic. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec07-F05 | anchor: A61
When multiple lanes permit the same turn, keep the corresponding lane through the turn until it is finished. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> pdf-0061]

Source: [A62 -> pdf-0062]

Mnemonic: observe, signal, find space, recheck, complete.
Glossary: a blind spot is an area that vehicle structure or mirrors prevent you from seeing. [A63]
Dynamic facts: municipal restrictions and current penalty amounts retain their local and dated scope.

## C2 — General Driving

FACT_ID: sec07-R01 | anchor: A67
Before passing, anticipate users moving into your space because of roadside people, cyclists, a narrow bridge, ice, damaged pavement or an obstruction. [A67]
Source: [A67 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec07-R02 | anchor: A67
Begin passing only with known return space, without assuming several vehicles can be passed or that other drivers will make room. [A67]
Source: [A67 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec07-R03 | anchor: A68
Complete a pass before reaching the start of a no-passing zone. [A68]
Source: [A68 -> pdf-0068]

Source: [A68 -> pdf-0068]

Source: [A73 -> pdf-0073]

Source: [A73 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec07-R50 | anchor: A73
In the forward method, stop once the rear clears the driveway edge, then check traffic, signal right and select reverse. [A73]
Source: [A73 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec07-R51 | anchor: A73

FACT_ID: sec07-R52 | anchor: A73

sections.heading: D — General Driving
sections.markdown:
## D — General Driving
Accuracy scope: General Driving facts use the pinned official PDF and one physical page per fact; original phrasing preserves actor qualifications, exceptions and modal verbs.
Expressway guidance prohibits right-side passing while the general road section lists right-pass exceptions. Preserve the road-specific text and verify overlap before portraying it as an exceptionless statutory rule. [A65]
Passing-time and total-distance figures are source illustrations, not guarantees that every vehicle can complete a safe pass within those values. [A66] [A67]
Bus stopping and release rules retain undivided versus physically divided roadway context and the driver-signal alternative where stated. The official bus diagram was inspected. [A69]
The distance/penalty list is introduced as some municipal ordinances. No hydrant, driveway or crosswalk distance from that list is generalized to every Maine municipality. [A70]
The hill-parking left/right instruction does not explicitly name the side of the street. Its safe roll-direction principle is retained; street-side-specific steering remains clarification debt. [A70]
Parking, access-aisle and turnaround pixels were inspected. No unprinted geometry or curb-color code is inferred, and parallel-parking points retain the vehicle-size caveat. [A70] [A71] [A72] [A73]
Confidence process: every drafted fact received a same-model source-context check before submission; independent coverage and hallucination QA remain pending.
Officeholders, telephone numbers and changing administrative details are excluded from stable learner statements. No source attribution is a legal or clinical signoff.

ranked.label: Before a turn, check controls, pedestrians and vehicles, signal, and enter the nearest lane in the intended direction.
Look through the turn as far as possible, accelerate smoothly and ensure the signal cancels afterward.
Start a right turn from the rightmost part of your lane without swinging left first.
Start a left turn from the leftmost part of your lane and yield to oncoming traffic.
When multiple lanes permit the same turn, keep the corresponding lane through the turn until it is finished.
An intersection is any meeting of traffic paths, including side streets, freeway entries and driveways or shopping-center entrances.
Look in both directions even when crossing a one-way street because a vehicle may be traveling the wrong way.
At intersections, slow and search for controls, traffic, pedestrians, cyclists, road conditions and blocked sight lines.
Check cross traffic even when it faces red or a stop sign, and be ready to yield to prevent a crash.
After stopping, check traffic and cyclists with a left-right-left search before entry.
Before moving on green, confirm the path is clear and cross traffic has stopped.
Do not enter a lane merely because an approaching driver signals a turn; the signal may be mistaken or refer to a later turn.
If a fixed obstruction blocks a cross-street view, edge forward slowly only far enough to see and wait for traffic to clear before turning.
If cars in one lane hide another lane, wait for them to pass rather than pushing the vehicle’s nose into the hidden lane.
Vehicles entering a circle or roundabout yield to circulating traffic unless police or a traffic-control device directs otherwise.
Enter a roundabout to the right of the center island and travel counterclockwise.
At the described small-island roundabout, raised inner pavement accommodates trucks while ordinary vehicles remain in the outer travel lane.
Exit a traffic circle with a right turn and pay close attention to signs and lane markings.
In the described rotary, a driver exiting within 2 exits is advised to use the rightmost lane unless signs or markings assign another lane.
Slow on entering a circle, yield to circulating traffic, follow lane lines and signal the exit.
A lane change requires mirror checks and a head turn toward the intended side to inspect the blind spot.
Blind spots include areas hidden by vehicle structure and areas the mirrors do not cover.
For a lane change, find a gap, signal, look again, adjust speed, move over and cancel the signal afterward.
Lane-change precautions also apply to freeway entry and moving onto a road from its curb or shoulder.
Before moving sideways, check mirrors for passing traffic and look over the relevant shoulder for vehicles near the rear corner.
Watch particularly for motorcycles and bicycles during a lane-change check.
Make rearward checks brief so your eyes return promptly to the road ahead.
Inspect every relevant lane because another driver may be moving toward the same gap.
Signal your intended movement at least 100 feet before making the change.
Use the expressway acceleration lane to approach traffic speed before merging, while looking for a suitable gap.
For the described expressway entry, signal left, check the rearview mirror and over the shoulder, merge into a clear gap and cancel the signal.
Where an expressway entrance lacks an acceleration lane, stop before entry, wait for a traffic gap, then accelerate and merge.
Traffic already on an expressway need not yield to entering traffic, so avoid merging at a speed that obstructs its flow.
The expressway guidance says to remain in the right lane unless passing and not to pass on the right or shoulder.
Before expressway passing, signal, check mirrors and look over the shoulder to confirm clearance.
Do not increase speed while another vehicle is passing you.
Pass promptly and safely, avoid lingering alongside, and return right only after the entire passed vehicle appears in the rearview mirror.
Avoid cruising in the neighboring driver’s blind spot.
For an expressway exit, move right early and signal; begin slowing in the deceleration lane rather than the through lane.
Slow to the ramp’s posted speed and ensure the exit signal cancels.
Stop on an expressway only for an emergency; signal and pull as far off the pavement as the shoulder allows.
Raise the hood to request help after the described emergency stop.
Never reverse, walk or stand on an expressway’s traveled portion.
Long straight highway travel can cause drowsiness or reduced awareness, so continued concentration is essential.
The manual’s alertness tips include a cool cabin, scanning ahead, conversation or music and small speed variations.
At the first drowsiness warning, use the nearest rest or service area to stretch, nap or change drivers if possible.
Do not depend on stay-awake drugs to make tired driving safe.
Passing on a two-lane road uses the opposing lane, so signal and start only when it is clear.
The manual gives 10 to 12 seconds as a passing-time guide at 50 to 55 miles per hour.
Assess passing space before an approaching vehicle, hill, curve, intersection or road obstruction.
Before passing, check oncoming traffic, mirrors and the shoulder blind spot, signal and enter the left passing lane.
After passing, wait until the whole vehicle is visible in the rearview mirror, signal and shoulder-check before returning right.
After returning to the right lane, adjust speed and cancel the passing signal.
When being passed, remain in your lane and keep a steady speed.
If an overtaker abandons the pass and drops behind, you may need to increase speed before an oncoming vehicle arrives.
The highway-passing illustration allows over 1,600 feet, roughly one-third mile, for the combined opposing vehicles’ travel.
A distant oncoming vehicle can appear nearly stationary while already being too close for a pass.
Do not start passing within one-third mile of a hill or curve that blocks the view ahead.
Avoid passing at intersections, crossroads or shopping-center entries where traffic or people may enter the road.
Do not pass while approaching a railroad crossing or bridge.
Before passing, anticipate users moving into your space because of roadside people, cyclists, a narrow bridge, ice, damaged pavement or an obstruction.
Begin passing only with known return space, without assuming several vehicles can be passed or that other drivers will make room.
Complete a pass before reaching the start of a no-passing zone.
Do not pass when the center line on your side is solid.
A broken center line on your side permits passing only when no oncoming vehicles occupy the passing lane.
A yellow No Passing Zone pennant on the left or a white Do Not Pass sign on the right prohibits passing there.
When passing a cyclist, slow down and leave at least 3 feet between the vehicle’s right side and the bicycle.
On school property, an undivided road or a Maine parking area, stop for a school bus displaying flashing red lights when approaching from either direction.
After stopping for the described school bus, wait while children board or leave and proceed only when the bus moves or its driver signals permission.
On a divided road, stop for a school bus’s flashing red lights or extended stop arm unless a solid divider separates your roadway from the bus.
In the divided-road bus guidance, proceed slowly while watching for children after the red lights stop and the stop arm is no longer visible.
Park so the vehicle creates no hazard or interference with public-road traffic.
Park parallel to the road unless painted angle-parking lines indicate otherwise.
Leave at least 2 feet between your parked vehicle and vehicles ahead or behind.
Use a marked parking area and move as far out of travel lanes as available shoulder space permits.
Beside a curb, park as close as practical and no farther than 18 inches away.
Secure a parked vehicle with its parking brake and park gear, or first or reverse gear for a manual transmission.
For hill parking, arrange the wheels so an unintended roll is stopped by the curb, or without a curb moves off the road rather than into traffic.
Exit on the curb side when possible; before opening a traffic-side door, look behind for vehicles and especially bicycles.
When leaving the car, switch off the engine and remove the key, and lock it if it will be out of sight.
Under the described municipal restrictions, reserved disability parking requires the appropriate permit or plates.
The manual lists a $100 state-law fine for misuse of disability plates or placards.
A municipality may prohibit parking in loading zones.
The municipal examples prohibit parking within 10 feet of a hydrant where that ordinance applies.
The municipal examples prohibit parking within 15 feet of a fire-station driveway or directly opposite its entrance.
The municipal examples prohibit parking within 15 feet of a crosswalk.
Municipal restrictions may reserve public-place entrances from parking during designated hours.
Using a disability space with an access aisle requires displaying a disability plate or placard and using the aisle for vehicle entry or exit, such as with a lift or mobility device.
Parking in an access aisle is prohibited, and misuse is a traffic infraction with a fine of at least $200.
Check signs and painted curbs for parking prohibitions or limits.
To enter an angle or perpendicular space, check traffic, signal, center the vehicle and stop at the front of the space.
When leaving an angle or perpendicular space, keep checking traffic and reverse until the front bumper clears the neighboring vehicle.
After that clearance, steer toward the desired rearward direction, stop once clear of the space, select drive and move ahead.
For the described parallel-parking setup, check traffic and signal, then align beside the car ahead of the space about 2 feet away.
In the parallel-parking method, select reverse only when clear, look rearward and turn right while backing slowly.
In that method, straighten the wheels after the front door passes the forward car’s rear bumper, then continue backing straight.
Once clear of the forward car, steer left while backing and stop before touching the rear vehicle.
Steer right and pull forward to center the vehicle in the parallel space; straighten the wheels unless parked on a hill.
After parallel parking, aim for about 6 inches from the curb and never exceed 18 inches.
The described parking reference points may require adjustment for the vehicle’s size.
To leave a parallel space, check traffic, brake and back near the rear vehicle, then signal, select drive and move forward slowly.
Before steering out of a parallel space, confirm the front bumper clears the forward car; otherwise reverse and readjust.
In the described parallel-space exit, move promptly into the lane once the doorpost clears the forward car’s rear bumper.
From a right-side parking position, look over the left shoulder; from a left curb, look over the right shoulder before entering traffic.
Signal and pull out slowly only when the destination lane is clear for a safe distance.
When going around the block is unavailable, a street, alley or driveway may serve for a two-point turnaround.
For a reverse two-point turnaround, check behind, signal right and drive 1 car length beyond the driveway before looking over the right shoulder and backing into it.
After backing into the driveway for that turnaround, select drive, check traffic and turn left into the proper lane only when clear, with a left signal.
For a forward two-point turnaround, check oncoming traffic, signal left and turn into the drive or alley near its right side.
In the forward method, stop once the rear clears the driveway edge, then check traffic, signal right and select reverse.
When clear, back with a sharp right steer, straighten and stop centered in the lane, then select drive and cancel the signal.
Use a three-point turnaround only on a two-lane road too narrow for a U-turn, preferring a trip around the block where possible.
Begin the three-point method by checking mirrors, signaling right and stopping at the road’s right side.
Next signal left, check traffic and the left blind spot, and when clear turn sharply left across the road and stop.
Then select reverse, check traffic and both blind spots, and when clear steer sharply right while backing across and stop.
Finish by selecting drive, signaling left and checking traffic and blind spots before moving into the right lane in the new direction, then cancel the signal.
